Alger, 12 septembre 2026 (Algeria Tech): Algiers, September 12, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he is ready to slow down the development of his technologies provided that competitors commit to a collective moratorium. This move follows multiple warnings from specialists regarding the existential risks associated with these technologies.
Proposition de moratoire collectif par S: Proposal for a collective moratorium by Sam Altman
Lors d'une réunion interne organisée cet: During an internal meeting held this week, the OpenAI leader told employees that the company could moderate the pace of its innovations, according to Reuters reports. However, Sam Altman advocates for a coordinated suspension of research with all competing laboratories. This consultation aims to prevent an isolated player from losing ground to rivals who are less rigorous about safety.
Cette prise de position intervient alors: This stance comes as OpenAI and its competitor Anthropic prepare for their initial public offerings on Wall Street. Although the start-up recently temporarily suspended its most advanced projects before launching its new Astra model for ChatGPT, the financial calendar makes a unilateral slowdown complex for the company.
Mobilisation et alertes au sein de l'ind: Mobilization and warnings within the AI industry
Plusieurs initiatives récentes témoignen: Several recent initiatives reflect a desire for regulation within the tech sector. An open letter signed by OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and more than one hundred companies calls for an urgent global response to the risks of AI-facilitated cyberattacks. Additionally, more than a thousand industry employees have signed a petition calling for a mechanism to control the pace of development.
Le PDG d'OpenAI, Sam Altman, propose un: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is proposing a shared moratorium with competitors to slow down the development of artificial intelligence.
OpenAI refuse de freiner ses recherches: OpenAI refuses to curb its research unilaterally for fear of losing ground to rivals less rigorous on safety.
Une lettre signée par OpenAI, Google, An: A letter signed by OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and more than one hundred companies calls for global action against the threats of AI-generated cyberattacks.
Une pétition rassemblant plus de mille s: A petition gathering more than a thousand employees from the AI industry is demanding the establishment of a system to regulate the pace of development.
Jacob Coxon, chercheur ayant travaillé t: Jacob Coxon, a researcher who worked for three years at OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned on September 9, 2026, denouncing the lack of accountability of both firms.
Le responsable de la sécurité d'Anthropi: Anthropic's head of safety, Evan Hubinger, estimates at more than ten percent the probability that AI will cause the extinction of humanity within a decade.
